card.title: Believe This with Me
card.instruction: Recruit someone into treating your impossible explanation as the most useful version of events.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The office kettle's on strike. Help me negotiate before the clients arrive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've filled it twice. It still won't boil.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then water isn't its grievance. Tell it we'll stop leaving it alone after meetings.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can take it into the meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Give it my chair. A seat at the table should get us tea.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 asks negotiation; A3 interprets water failure as a different grievance and A5 assigns A's chair to win tea.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 refilling failed, shaping A3 a social grievance; B4 taking kettle to the meeting leads A5 formal inclusion at the table.

relationship.evidence: B2 has attempted practical repair and B4 offers a feasible inclusion action, actively developing A's game.

heightening.evidence: B4 cooperation becomes A5 a fuller recognition demand with a direct desired result, tea for clients.
